threads.thread_goal: Align on candidate dishes and lock the final seasonal lunch menu list.

messages.text: Sharing the first pass of the Seasonal Lunch Menu Draft for the project_title now. It is in A1 and covers 10 ideas mapped to T1: 3 meat, 2 fish, 3 vegetarian, 2 vegan. All are built around what we already do well: grain bowls, soups, and salads, plus one hot sandwich. Please have a look today and comment on what feels realistic for a 21‑day rollout, especially from a prep and service point of view.

Had a first read through A1. From a workflow angle, the grain bowls and soups look the safest. The hot sandwich might slow the pass if we are not careful with holding and toasting. Also, we only have two vegan options right now. For a healthy seasonal focus, I would lean toward at least three vegetarian and two vegan on the final list. How many total dishes are we aiming for on the board at lunch?

I like the balance in A1 overall. The roasted veg grain bowl and the lentil soup look quick to batch and reheat safely. The fish dishes might be tight on timing if we cook them fully to order. Maybe we can keep just one fish main and make sure it shares garnish and sauces with one of the meat dishes to keep the line simple.

I can help with the salads and sandwiches from A1. The chicken salad bowl and the hummus veg bowl look fine to prep with what we have. I am a bit unsure about the baked fish dish, it might need more oven space than we have at peak. Maybe we keep the fish as a lighter option, like the fish salad, instead of a full hot plate.

On total dish count, if we keep it to 8 for lunch service it should be manageable with our current equipment. Maybe 3 meat or fish, 3 vegetarian, 2 vegan. That would also help us keep T1 tight and not overcomplicate the first season. We can always rotate one or two items later once we see sales and waste.

Agree that 8 dishes is a good ceiling for launch. Proposal: 2 meat, 1 fish, 3 vegetarian, 2 vegan. That keeps the board readable and gives enough plant‑forward options. If we go with that, we would need to drop two of the current meat or fish ideas from A1. My suggestion is to keep the chicken grain bowl and the turkey hot sandwich, and choose only one fish dish, probably the baked fish with seasonal greens if we can manage oven space.

If we cap at 8, I support the 2 meat, 1 fish, 3 vegetarian, 2 vegan split. That gives us five plant‑based dishes on the board, which fits the healthy angle. On the fish, I would actually lean toward the lighter fish salad instead of the baked fish. It uses less oven time and we can share prep with the chicken salad bowl. That will help with timing risk during the 21‑day rollout.

I am ok with the fish salad instead of the baked fish. That will also make allergen handling a bit easier at the pass. For the vegetarian and vegan slots, I would keep: roasted veg grain bowl, lentil soup, stuffed peppers, hummus veg bowl, and the quinoa salad. That gives us a mix of hot and cold and uses ingredients we already buy.

Just to check, with that list we would have: chicken grain bowl, turkey hot sandwich, fish salad, roasted veg grain bowl, lentil soup, stuffed peppers, hummus veg bowl, quinoa salad. That is 8 dishes. I can start thinking about standard portions for the bowls once we confirm this is the final list.

That list looks good to me. It also keeps the hot line to three items, which is safer for space and holding. For the vegan count, hummus veg bowl and quinoa salad are clearly vegan. Stuffed peppers could be vegan if we avoid cheese or use a plant‑based filling. Do we want to lock that in so we definitely have three vegetarian and two vegan as discussed?

I would keep stuffed peppers as vegetarian with cheese, and rely on hummus veg bowl and quinoa salad as the two vegan dishes. That still gives us three vegetarian items: roasted veg grain bowl, lentil soup, stuffed peppers. So we hit the 3 vegetarian and 2 vegan target without overcomplicating substitutions.

Summing up so we can move T1 forward: final candidate list for full recipe work is chicken grain bowl, turkey hot sandwich, fish salad, roasted veg grain bowl, lentil soup, stuffed peppers, hummus veg bowl, quinoa salad. That is 8 dishes total, with 2 meat, 1 fish, 3 vegetarian, 2 vegan. Unless anyone objects today, I will treat this as the locked list for recipe development.
No objections from me. That mix feels balanced and realistic for the line. I will start sketching basic ingredient lists for the lentil soup and stuffed peppers so we are ready when we open T2.
Works for me too. I will wait for the recipe templates before I write anything up, but I can start testing portion sizes on the grain bowls during prep this week.
All good from my side. Once we have the recipes, I can help check that the sandwich and bowls fit our current holding equipment so we do not break the service window.

threads.thread_goal: Define recipes, portions, and costing for each approved dish.

messages.text: First version of the Standard Recipe Cards Pack and costing sheet is ready. A2 has draft recipes for all 8 agreed dishes, and A3 has initial costing based on current supplier prices. This covers T2 and T3 at a first pass. Please review portions and any ingredients that look risky on cost or availability.

I went through A2 and A3. Most dishes are close to target, but two stand out: the turkey hot sandwich and the quinoa salad. The turkey portion is a bit generous for lunch, and the quinoa price has gone up. If we reduce turkey by 20 grams and swap half the quinoa for pearl barley, we should bring both dishes back into the food cost range without hurting the healthy positioning.

On portions, the grain bowls in A2 are set at 120 grams cooked grain, 100 grams veg, and 80 grams protein. That feels filling but might be heavy for some guests. If we standardise at 100 grams grain and keep veg high, we can keep the plate looking full and help with cost control in A3.

I tried plating one of the bowls with the current A2 portions and it did look quite big. I can test the 100 grams grain version during prep and see how it looks in the regular bowl. That might also make it easier to keep portions consistent on a busy shift.

Swapping half the quinoa for barley in the salad sounds fine to me, as long as we keep the dressing bright. For the turkey sandwich, reducing the meat slightly is ok if we keep plenty of salad and a good spread. We should just make sure the recipe card in A2 is very clear on slice count so no one overbuilds it.

Good points. Proposal for standard portions to plug into A2 and A3: bowls at 100 grams cooked grain, 120 grams mixed veg, 80 grams protein; soups at 300 ml per portion; salads at 120 grams base plus toppings as listed; sandwich with 80 grams turkey, standard bread, and veg garnish. If we agree on this, I will update A2 and recalc A3.

I am comfortable with those portion numbers. They should keep us within the target food cost once we apply the turkey reduction and the quinoa and barley mix. We just need to be strict on using the correct scoops and ladles during service.
Agreed on the standard portions. I will adjust the lentil soup and stuffed peppers recipes in A2 to match the 300 ml soup portion and the veg and grain ratios you listed.
Ok for me too. Once you update A2, I will follow the new scoops for the bowls and note if anything feels off during prep.

On the ingredient swaps: turkey down by 20 grams and half quinoa replaced with barley both sound workable. Do we need to consider any other substitutions, like switching one of the nuts in the quinoa salad to seeds, or is that more of an allergen topic for later?

From a cost angle, the main substitutions we need now are the turkey reduction and the quinoa and barley mix. Nuts versus seeds is more about allergens and menu positioning, so I would leave that for the allergen sheet and front‑of‑house wording. For budget, I suggest we formally approve these two changes so A2 and A3 can be finalised.
Noted. I will update A2 with the standard portions and the two approved substitutions, then refresh A3 with the new quantities. Once that is done, T2 and T3 will be ready for the tasting phase.

threads.thread_goal: Set up prep workflow, food safety checklist, and allergen reference.

messages.text: Here is a summary of the proposed daily prep schedule for the new menu, plus first drafts of the prep and safety checklist and the allergen sheet. A4 covers the cleaning and critical control points, A6 lists allergens and dietary tags per dish. This is the first pass on T4, T6, and T9. Please check timings, storage steps, and allergen flags carefully.

Looking at the schedule in T4: morning prep has both soups and roasted veg in the oven at the same time. That might be tight for space. I suggest we roast veg first, then do soups, and use the chilling step in A4 to bring soups down safely before service. Also, in A6, the quinoa salad is marked as gluten free, but with the barley substitution it should be updated.

For responsibilities in T4, I propose we split like this: one person on soups and sauces, one on grains and roasted veg, one on salads and cold prep. That way we avoid everyone crowding the same station. We should also add a note in A4 about labelling and dating all batched items for the new menu.

I am happy to take salads and cold prep on the schedule. It would help me if A4 clearly lists which items must be kept on the top shelf in the walk‑in and which can go lower, so I do not mix anything up.

Good catch on the barley. In A6, quinoa salad should be marked as containing gluten once we confirm the mix. Also, for the hummus veg bowl, we need to make sure sesame is clearly flagged. I see it in the ingredients but the allergen column is blank.

On storage, we can add to A4 that ready‑to‑eat salads and cooked grains for cold dishes stay on the top shelves, raw meat on the bottom, and soups and roasted veg in the middle, covered and labelled. That should keep cross‑contamination risk low.

I will adjust T4 so veg roasting happens first, then soups, with chilling steps as per A4. For responsibilities, I like the split that was suggested: soups and sauces, grains and roasted veg, salads and cold prep. If everyone is ok with that, we can lock the daily prep schedule and roles.

Works for me. I can take soups and sauces on most days and back up grains and veg when needed. The schedule in T4 just needs clear times for when each batch should be in the oven so we do not slip into service.

I am fine with being on salads and cold prep. Having it written in T4 will help me plan my morning. Please just highlight any items that need extra care for allergens so I do not prep them next to each other.

On A6, I will update quinoa salad to show gluten due to barley, and mark sesame for the hummus veg bowl. I will also double‑check the 14 major allergens for each dish against the ingredient lists in A2 before we print the sheet.
I will do a second pass on A6 once you have updated it, focusing on dairy, gluten, nuts, and sesame. If we both review it against A2, we should be confident that front‑of‑house can rely on it.

Once the allergen sheet in A6 is final, can we also add a simple note in A4 that any changes to ingredients must be written on the sheet the same day? That will help avoid gaps if we ever need to substitute something.
Sounds good. I will push an updated A6 today with the barley and sesame corrections and a full allergen check. After your review, we can treat that version as the single reference for service.

threads.thread_goal: Run tasting, refine recipes, and lock plating and service guidelines.

messages.text: Thanks for the internal tasting today. I have uploaded the notes and timing results into A7 and added a first draft of the plating and service guide in A5. This covers the first loop on T7 and T5. Please share any strong reactions from the tasting and check that the plating steps are realistic for a busy lunch.

From the tasting notes in A7: the lentil soup flavour was good but a bit thick by the end of service, and the turkey sandwich took slightly longer than target to assemble. I suggest we loosen the soup with a bit more stock and pre‑slice the turkey to the exact portion size, as long as we keep it chilled properly. For plating in A5, we should also simplify the garnish on the fish salad to one herb instead of two.

I agree with the soup feedback. During the run in T7, it held well for the first hour but thickened later. I can adjust the recipe in A2 to add a bit more liquid and note a gentle top‑up with hot stock between services. On plating, the roasted veg grain bowl looked good but took a few extra seconds because of the scattered seeds. Maybe we can keep them to one sprinkle point instead of two.

I struggled a bit with the quinoa salad plating from A5. The layers were hard to keep neat when it was busy. It might be easier if we mix the base and then just top with veg and seeds, instead of trying to keep three separate rings in the bowl.

On the turkey sandwich timing, pre‑slicing to portion size will help a lot. We should also check that the build order in A5 is clear: spread, leaves, turkey, veg, then close and press. That way everyone does it the same way and we avoid overfilling.

I will update A2 and A5 based on this: slightly more stock in the lentil soup, clear note on gentle top‑up; pre‑sliced turkey portions with storage guidance; simplified garnish on the fish salad; and a simpler quinoa salad plating with mixed base and a single seed sprinkle. Any other recipe changes from A7 before we lock the adjustments?

One more from A7: the hummus veg bowl was slightly salty when we added olives on top. I would reduce salt in the hummus base a little and keep the olives as the main salty element. Otherwise, I am happy with the recipe tweaks you listed.
I can take care of the hummus adjustment in A2 and note it in T8. I will also make sure the salt level is written clearly so we do not drift back up over time.
With the simpler quinoa salad plating and fewer garnish steps on the bowls, I feel more confident about keeping pace. The photos in A5 will help a lot once they are updated.

For the final plating standards in A5, can we also add a short service note per dish, like which ones can be held a few minutes on the pass and which must go straight out? That will help us and front‑of‑house coordinate during busy periods.

Great, thanks. Once the hummus salt adjustment and soup liquid changes are in A2 and logged in A7, I will mark those as the final recipes for launch. That will close the tasting adjustment loop for T7 and T8.

I will help refine the service notes in A5: which dishes can wait briefly, which must go immediately, and any last‑minute checks like stirring soup or re‑tossing salads. Once those are in, I think we can sign off the plating and service guide.
Perfect. After those notes are added, we will treat the current A5 as the final plating and service standard for launch, including photos and build order for each dish.

threads.thread_goal: Plan launch week operations and agree on tracking of sales and waste.

messages.text: Sharing the draft launch week service plan and the sales and waste log template. The plan outlines expected volumes, backup options, and a slightly reduced menu for the first two days. A8 is the log we will use for T12, and the plan ties into T11. Please review and confirm the launch date and any temporary menu reductions.

Looking at the plan in T11, I think launching on a Tuesday gives us Monday to prep and train. For the first two days, I would keep all 8 dishes but limit batch sizes on the fish salad and quinoa salad until we see demand. As backups, we can lean on our existing tomato soup and a simple grilled cheese if anything fails.

Tuesday launch works for me. On the reduced menu idea, do we want to hide any dishes from the board on day one, or just quietly prep fewer portions of the more complex ones? I would prefer to keep the full board visible if we can handle it.
For A8, I understand we need to log portions sold and waste daily, but I am not sure when exactly to fill it in. Is the idea that whoever closes lunch service updates the sheet before cleaning down?

I would suggest we note rough sales during service on a small tally sheet at the pass, then the person on salads and cold prep updates A8 right after service, before we start deep cleaning. That way we do not forget numbers once it gets busy.

I am also in favour of keeping all 8 dishes on the board from day one, but with smaller initial batches for fish salad and quinoa salad as suggested. If we agree on Tuesday as launch day, we can use Monday for a short run‑through with front‑of‑house and a final check of A6 and A5.

Tuesday launch with full board and smaller first batches sounds good. For backups, I will make sure the plan in T11 clearly lists tomato soup and grilled cheese as fallbacks if any new dish runs out or has an issue.
All good from my side. I will be on soups and sauces that week, so I will keep an eye on the tomato soup backup and note any issues in the end‑of‑day recap.

On A8 usage, proposal: during service we keep a simple tally sheet at the pass; after lunch, the salads and cold prep person enters portions sold and waste into A8; then whoever is closing quickly checks that the totals look reasonable. If we all follow that, T12 will give us clean data from day one.
That works for me. I can take care of filling in A8 on the days I am on salads and cold prep, as long as the tally sheet is clear.
I am fine with that routine too. Maybe we can add a small note in T12 that the tally sheet stays by the pass printer so everyone knows where to find it.
With that process, we should get reliable sales and waste data without slowing down closing. I suggest we confirm this as the standard way of using A8 during launch week.

Great. To recap: we launch on Tuesday with the full 8‑dish board, smaller first batches for fish salad and quinoa salad, tomato soup and grilled cheese as backups, and A8 updated daily by the salads and cold prep person using the tally sheet from the pass. I will update T11 and T12 to reflect this.
